reproduction_target: Derivation and application of a method for computing reliabilities, standard errors and frequentist p-values of SNP marker effect estimates within a single-step SNP-BLUP (ssSNPBLUP) genomic evaluation, applied to two German national routine evaluation datasets: German Limousin (LIM) beef cattle weaning weight (200-day weight, multi-trait maternal effect animal BLUP model, December 2023 routine run) and German Holstein (HOL) production traits (milk yield, protein yield, fat yield, somatic cell score, random regression test-day model). The computational chain is: routine ssSNPBLUP genomic evaluation in the Mix99 software suite -> stepwise absorption of fixed and non-genetic random effects into animal effects to obtain Interbull-style effective record contributions (ERC) of cows and effective daughter contributions (EDC) of bulls -> inversion of the reduced mixed model equation coefficient matrix to obtain prediction error (co)variances of SNP effect estimates -> per-SNP reliability, standard error, Z score and Normal-distribution p-value -> significance thresholding (base 0.05, Bonferroni 0.05/45613 = 5.9 on the -log10 scale, and an arbitrary 0.10% of total genetic variance explained) -> comparison against a conventional single-marker-regression GWAS on deregressed proofs computed in GCTA (LIM only) -> Manhattan plots and per-chromosome SNP reliability distributions. There are no wet-lab steps: all inputs are pre-existing routine national evaluation phenotype, pedigree and genotype databases held by vit Verden.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML (retrieved by curl to a unique local path; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403, and a shared /tmp filename was clobbered by a concurrent job, so the final extraction was re-run and re-verified against this DOI's own file — 102,266 bytes XML, 40,677 characters of stripped text). Only two pieces of software are named in the entire paper: 'The ssSNPBLUP model was implemented in the Mix99 suite of software [25], the single marker regression GWAS approach was implemented in GCTA [22].' Neither carries a version. A full-text regex search for github/gitlab/bitbucket/zenodo/figshare/softwareheritage/osf/dryad returned ZERO matches, and a search for the literal strings 'version'/'Version' returned zero hits referring to any software. The Availability of data and materials statement is verbatim: 'The data supporting this study's findings may be available upon request from vit Verden. However, restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under a licence of a material transfer agreement for the current study and thus are not publicly available.' The Authors' contributions statement is the only mention of code: 'DA and ZL wrote the code for the analysis.' — with no repository. W = 0: this is a pure-computational methods-and-application paper with no physical steps.

steps.label: Routine single-step SNP-BLUP (ssSNPBLUP) genomic evaluation of German Limousin 200-day weaning weight, implemented in the Mix99 software suite [25] — standard multi-trait maternal effect animal model [23] with fixed effects of season of birth, sex, birth type (single/twin), month of birth, and parity nested within dam age class; residual polygenic (RPG) effect with variance proportion k in (0,1); GEBVs and SNP effects estimated simultaneously; December 2023 routine beef cattle evaluation. No Mix99 version, no release, no control/parameter files, no solver settings, no convergence criterion, and no value of k stated

Routine ssSNPBLUP genomic evaluation of German Holstein production traits (milk yield, protein yield, fat yield, somatic cell score) under a random regression test-day model [24], 'described in detail by [17]' — model structure, covariate functions, fixed effect definitions and variance components are entirely deferred to the cited prior publication; Table 1 reports trait, breed, heritability, genetic variance and number of reference animals. No Mix99 version, no parameter files, no evaluation run date

Genotype preparation: 'The genotypic dataset is based on the Illumina V2 chip and the UMD 3.1 reference genome. The genotypes were imputed to a common panel of 45,613 markers across the 31 chromosomes of cattle.' No imputation software is named at all, no version, no reference/haplotype panel, no imputation accuracy filter, no call-rate / MAF / HWE quality-control thresholds, and no per-chromosome marker counts (deferred to [17])

Stepwise absorption of fixed effects b and non-genetic random effects p into the animal additive genetic effects to obtain Interbull-style effective record contributions (ERC) of phenotyped cows, followed by absorption of daughter ERC into sires (with adjustment for dam contributions) to obtain effective daughter contributions (EDC) of bulls, including the double-counting adjustment when genotyped cows and their genotyped sires both occur in the sub-population [18]. Stated to be 'similar to steps 7 and 8 in [9]'. Author-written code, not released; no software named for this step; the absorption algorithm and its numerical settings are deferred to Interbull methodology and to references [9] and [18]

Construction and inversion of the reduced mixed model equation (Eq. 6) over the genotyped-and-phenotyped sub-population to obtain prediction error (co)variances of the SNP effect estimates — pseudo-phenotypes y*, general mean, R^-1 = diag(phi) with phi the EDC/ERC weights, variance ratio built from trait heritability h^2, and C^gg the submatrix of the inverse associated with SNP effects [19]. The equation system is fully written out in the paper. RPG is explicitly excluded from Eq. (6) ('the computation would have become too heavy and infeasible') and reintroduced only at the standard-error stage. No solver, library, linear-algebra backend, or numerical tolerance is named, and no code is released

Per-SNP reliability, standard error, Z score and p-value computation (Eqs. 7-12): reliability of the j-th marker effect from C^gg and the average additive genetic variance per SNP under the equal-variance infinitesimal assumption (average SNP variance = var(DGV)/sum(2pq)); SE_j from the RPG-adjusted average SNP variance; Z score = effect/SE; p-value from the standard Normal cumulative distribution function. All formulas are given explicitly in the prose. No software, no library, no version, no released code

Significance thresholding and significant-SNP counting — base rejection threshold p < 0.05 and Bonferroni-adjusted threshold 0.05/45,613 (= 5.9 on the -log10 scale) applied to both the ssSNPBLUP and the single-marker-regression p-values, plus a parallel 'arbitrary threshold of 0.10% of total genetic variance explained by a single marker' [9] used for cross-checking. Thresholds are numerically explicit and the resulting counts are reported (MY 2,239 / PY 1,629 / FY 964 / SCS 425 at p<0.05; MY 106 / PY 39 / FY 42 / SCS 8 at the Bonferroni threshold). No script released

Conventional pedigree-based BLUP evaluation of the LIM beef cattle dataset to estimate EBVs, followed by deregression of those EBVs using the matrix deregression approach [20, 21] to obtain 200-DW deregressed proofs used as the GWAS response. No software is named for either the pedigree BLUP run or the deregression, no version, no weighting/reliability-floor parameters, and no code released

Conventional single-marker-regression GWAS on the LIM deregressed proofs, 'implemented in GCTA [22]' — the model is written out (y* = 1*mu + standardized genotype matrix with elements built from allele counts and allele frequency p_j, per [22]). No GCTA version, no GCTA subcommand or option set (mlma / mlma-loco / fastGWA not specified), no GRM construction settings, no covariate list, no MAF filter, and no code released. The paper explicitly states this analysis could not be run for HOL: 'Due to the large reference population size, a conventional single marker regression GWAS could not be carried out for the HOL dataset.'

Figure generation — Manhattan plots of SNP effects in genetic standard deviations and of -log10 p-values for LIM 200-DW and for the four HOL production traits (Figs. 1-4), and per-chromosome distributions of SNP reliability for LIM 200-DW and HOL milk yield (Figs. 5-6). No plotting software, language, package, version, or script is named anywhere in the paper, and the plotting inputs (per-SNP effect, reliability and p-value tables) are not deposited

headline.static_readiness: 0/10 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI ceiling on 8/10 computational steps and X on the remaining 2 — the highest verdict attainable anywhere in this paper at Stage 1 is NI, and it would remain NI at Stage 2 because the blocking gaps are not code-inspection gaps. Not one software version is pinned anywhere in the paper: the only two named tools, the Mix99 suite [25] and GCTA [22], are cited by reference alone, and a full-text search for the strings 'version'/'Version' returns no hit referring to software. capture_claim is therefore 'none' — no lockfile, no container, no conda specification, no release tag, not even a floating version number. The statistical core (Eqs. 6-12: the reduced MME, prediction error variances, per-SNP reliability, standard error, Z score, Normal p-value) is written out completely enough to score params = 2 on C5-C7, which is the paper's genuine strength as a methods contribution — but the code that implements it is stated to exist ('DA and ZL wrote the code for the analysis') and is not released in any form, and the two datasets are national routine-evaluation databases explicitly withheld ('not publicly available', licence + material transfer agreement, 'may be available upon request from vit Verden'), so data caps at 1 (controlled) for every step. Two steps are blocked outright: C3, the imputation of genotypes to the common 45,613-marker panel, names no software and no QC threshold at all, and it is the step that produces the marker set on which every downstream p-value and Bonferroni correction (0.05/45,613) depends; and C10, all six figures, names no plotting toolchain and deposits no per-SNP result table. Nothing about this paper could gain R-star at Stage 2.
headline.coverage: 10 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods and Dataset sections, covering the full chain from routine ssSNPBLUP genomic evaluation (LIM and HOL) and genotype panel preparation through EDC/ERC absorption, PEV computation, per-SNP reliability/SE/Z/p-value derivation, significance thresholding, the comparator pedigree-BLUP + deregression + GCTA GWAS on LIM, and figure generation. W = 0: there are no wet-lab or physical-measurement steps in this paper — all inputs are pre-existing national routine evaluation phenotype, pedigree and genotype records. Coverage of the computational chain is complete at prose level; nothing in Methods was left unstepped.

gaps.where: Whole paper — no Code availability statement (steps C1-C10)
gaps.missing: The paper has no Code availability section. The only reference to code anywhere is in Authors' contributions, verbatim: 'DA and ZL wrote the code for the analysis.' A full-text search of the JATS XML for github, gitlab, bitbucket, zenodo, figshare, osf, dryad and Software Heritage returned zero matches. The central contribution of the paper is an algorithm — the stepwise EDC/ERC absorption, the reduced MME of Eq. (6), its inversion, and the reliability/SE/Z/p-value derivation of Eqs. (7)-(12) — and the implementation of that algorithm is precisely what is not released. No Mix99 control/parameter files, no absorption code, no inversion driver, no p-value script, and no plotting script are provided.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the analysis implementation (the absorption code producing EDC/ERC, the Eq. 6 assembly and inversion driver, the reliability/SE/Z/p-value computation, the GCTA invocation, and the figure scripts) in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo, and add a Code availability statement citing the DOI. Because Mix99 is licensed software, at minimum the Mix99 control files and parameter cards should be released even if the solver binary cannot be.

gaps.where: Steps C1-C10 — no software version pinned anywhere in the paper
gaps.missing: Zero version pins. The Mix99 suite (C1, C2) is cited as reference [25] with no release, build or year; GCTA (C9) is cited as reference [22] with no version and no subcommand. No software at all is named for genotype imputation (C3), for the absorption step (C4), for the linear algebra of the Eq. (6) inversion (C5), for the p-value computation (C6, C7), for the pedigree BLUP and matrix deregression (C8), or for the six figures (C10). No programming language, no numerical library, no BLAS/LAPACK, no operating system. This alone caps every step at NI regardless of what a Stage-2 code inspection would find.
gaps.how_to_close: State an exact version (or build identifier / commit) for every piece of software used, including the Mix99 release, the GCTA version, the imputation software, and the language and numerical libraries used for the custom absorption, inversion and p-value code. Note the reference genome as UMD 3.1 is pinned, which is good practice and should be extended to the software layer.

gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed: no lockfile, no container image or digest, no conda/renv/Docker specification, no sessionInfo(), no compiler or MPI configuration for what is described as a very large-scale computation ('the dimension of the MME system exceeded hundreds of millions for most dairy traits in German Holstein breed'). capture_claim = 'none'. There is no dependency closure and nothing to reconstruct one from.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a container image (with digest) or an environment lockfile covering the Mix99 runtime, GCTA, the imputation toolchain, and the language/numeric stack used for the custom code, and record the hardware and parallelization settings used for the large-scale HOL run.

gaps.where: Steps C1-C10 — controlled/withheld input data, no accession
gaps.missing: The Availability of data and materials statement is verbatim: 'The data supporting this study's findings may be available upon request from vit Verden. However, restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under a licence of a material transfer agreement for the current study and thus are not publicly available.' There is no repository, no dataset identifier, no accession of any kind (a full-text search for GEO/GSE/SRA/ENA/ArrayExpress/dbGaP/EGA/figshare/Zenodo returned zero matches), no data access committee, and no documented application procedure — only a named custodian and a hedged 'may be'. Both the LIM December 2023 routine beef evaluation records and the German Holstein national production-trait records are national breeding-value-estimation databases. Additionally, no derived intermediate is deposited: the per-SNP effect, reliability, standard error and p-value tables that constitute the paper's actual results appear only inside Manhattan plots and a 19-row Table 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Register the datasets with a controlled-access repository or at minimum publish a dataset identifier, the named data access contact, the MTA template, and the expected turnaround for applications. Independently of the raw records, deposit the full per-SNP output tables (marker id, chromosome, position, effect in genetic SD, reliability, SE, Z, p-value) for all traits in both populations — these are not individual-identifying and would make the p-value method's results independently checkable.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C2, C3, C8, C9
gaps.missing: Parameter under-specification in the evaluation and comparator steps. C1: the residual polygenic variance proportion k is defined as any value in (0,1) but its actual value is never given, nor are the variance components of the multi-trait maternal effect model, the solver convergence criterion, or the pedigree depth/base-population definition. C2: the entire HOL random regression test-day model — covariate functions, knots, fixed effect definitions, variance components — is deferred to [17] and [24]. C3: no imputation parameters or QC thresholds whatsoever. C8: no deregression weighting scheme, reliability floor, or parent-average removal settings for the matrix deregression. C9: no GCTA subcommand, no GRM settings, no covariates, no MAF or call-rate filter.
gaps.how_to_close: State the value of k actually used, the variance components for both evaluations, the solver settings and convergence criteria, the imputation software and its QC thresholds, the deregression weighting scheme, and the exact GCTA command line.

gaps.where: Steps C2, C4, C5, C8 — method deferred to prior publications
gaps.missing: This paper's prose is not self-contained for several load-bearing steps. The HOL evaluation model is 'described in detail by [17]'; the absorption procedure is 'similar to steps 7 and 8 in [9]' with the double-counting adjustment deferred to [18]; the PEV/inverse notation follows [19]; the deregression follows [20, 21]; the per-chromosome marker counts are 'presented in [17]'. Reproducing the pipeline therefore requires reconstructing methods from at least five other papers, none of which is verified here, and reference [11] (the authors' own prior German beef cattle ssSNPBLUP evaluation) supplies the LIM evaluation context.
gaps.how_to_close: Restate the load-bearing details in this paper (the HOL model specification, the absorption algorithm steps, the deregression weighting) rather than only citing them, or publish a supplementary methods document that makes the chain self-contained.

gaps.missing: The parallel '0.10% of total genetic variance explained by a single marker' criterion is described by the authors themselves as 'an arbitrary threshold' [9], and the Discussion states plainly that 'the definition of what constitutes as a significant SNP can only be defined based on the aim of the study'. The choice of which SNPs are reported as significant therefore includes an analyst judgement that is not encoded in any script or rule file, and the cross-tabulation of the p-value approach against the variance-explained approach (e.g. the 42 of 106 MY SNPs recovered by both) depends on it.
gaps.how_to_close: Encode both thresholding rules in the released analysis script and publish the full per-SNP result table so that any alternative threshold can be applied by a reader without re-running the evaluation.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C2, C5 — computational feasibility as a stated barrier
gaps.missing: The paper repeatedly states that the exact computation is infeasible at national-evaluation scale ('inverting the full coefficient matrix of the MME is infeasible, because the dimension of the MME system exceeded hundreds of millions'; RPG omitted from Eq. (6) because 'the computation would have become too heavy'; the LIM-style single-marker GWAS 'could not be carried out for the HOL dataset'). Yet no compute environment, wall-clock time, memory footprint, node count, or parallelization scheme is reported for the approximation that was run. An independent reproducer cannot size the job, and cannot tell which approximation choices were driven by the resource envelope.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the compute environment (cores, memory, wall time, parallel framework) for both the LIM and HOL runs, and state the size of the reduced Eq. (6) system actually inverted in each case.
